title: What If a Tiny Black Hole Hit Earth?
description:
A black hole with the mass of a mountain (about a thousand trillion kilograms) would be smaller than an atom: its event horizon would be about a trillionth of a metre across. Moving at a typical space speed of a few hundred km/s, it would cross the whole Earth in about a minute, swallowing almost nothing. Physicists have calculated it would set off seismic waves like a small earthquake, and some are looking for exactly that signal.

Sources: Schwarzschild radius r = 2GM/c^2; Luo, Hanasoge, Tromp & Pretorius, "Detectable seismic consequences of the interaction of a primordial black hole with Earth", ApJ (2012).
Narration is AI-generated (ElevenLabs) and the pictures are AI-generated illustrations. This is a thought experiment.
